notes: The proof unjustifiably infers identical fair sex probabilities from independence and population balance. Counterexample: two two-child families have male indicators (X,Y) and (1-X,1-Y), with X,Y independent Bernoulli(3/4). Sexes are independent within each family, and every realization contains exactly two males and two females, yet expected brothers are 5/8 for males and 3/8 for females. Repeat these blocks for a large population. The draft avoids the documented strict-female-advantage pitfall.
